task:
Eliminate all wall-clock timing dependence from the unit test suite by converting the timing-sensitive tests to vitest fake timers. This repo just had a release (v0.23.27) fail CI on a timing flake in the per-source deadline test; the goal is that this class of flake can NEVER recur.

Files to convert (all under tests/unit/):
1. application/UpdateDocSets.test.ts - the 'per-source deadline' describe block: one test races a hung ingestor against a 500ms sourceDeadline with real timers and asserts `elapsed < 2000`; another uses a 300ms real setTimeout ingestor against a deadlineMs override. Convert to vi.useFakeTimers() + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync() so the deadline fires deterministically at fake-500ms regardless of CI load. The deadlineMs: 60_000 override on the fast source (added as a stopgap) can be simplified away once fake timers make the deadline deterministic.
2. shared/retry.test.ts - the delayFromError hint test asserts 70 <= elapsed < 500 against real time.
3. ingestors/GitIngestor.test.ts - 'retries transient clone failures with backoff' asserts elapsed >= 25 (real git spawns + real backoff sleeps).
4. ingestors/HttpIngestor.test.ts - the Retry-After test asserts elapsed >= 800 (real 1000ms wait).

How (researched against the vitest docs):
- vi.useFakeTimers() in the test (or beforeEach), vi.useRealTimers() in afterEach. Default toFake fakes Date too, so Date.now() becomes deterministic: it only advances when fake timers advance. Real async work (fs, child_process spawn, mocked fetch promises) still completes on the real event loop but does NOT move fake Date.
- Pattern: start the async operation WITHOUT awaiting it, then `await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(ms)` (or vi.runAllTimersAsync()) to fire the timer callbacks and flush microtasks, THEN await the operation promise. Never advance timers after already awaiting.
- Where jitter makes delays nondeterministic (backoffDelay adds raw * Math.random() * jitter), either pass jitter: 0 in the options or vi.spyOn(Math, 'random').mockReturnValue(0), then assert the EXACT delay (e.g. elapsed === 75, === 30, === 1000) instead of a range - fake Date makes this exact.
- Keep every behavioural assertion intact (status values, error messages, attempt counts, file counts). Do not weaken, skip, or delete any test. Do not touch src/ - this is a test-only refactor.

Done when: all four files use fake timers for their timing-sensitive tests, the full unit suite passes, and repeated runs are stable.

sensors.name: fake-timers
sensors.cmd: for f in tests/unit/application/UpdateDocSets.test.ts tests/unit/shared/retry.test.ts tests/unit/ingestors/GitIngestor.test.ts tests/unit/ingestors/HttpIngestor.test.ts; do rg -q 'useFakeTimers' "$f" || { echo "missing fake timers: $f"; exit 1; }; done
sensors.hint: Each of the four timing-sensitive test files must use vi.useFakeTimers() for its timing tests. See the task description for the exact pattern (start promise, advanceTimersByTimeAsync, then await).

sensors.name: stress
sensors.cmd: for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do npx vitest run tests/unit/application/UpdateDocSets.test.ts tests/unit/shared/retry.test.ts tests/unit/ingestors/GitIngestor.test.ts tests/unit/ingestors/HttpIngestor.test.ts >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "stress run $i failed"; exit 1; }; done
sensors.hint: The timing tests must pass 5 consecutive runs. If a run fails intermittently, a real wall-clock dependency remains - find it (rg -n 'Date.now|elapsed|setTimeout' the failing file) and convert it to fake timers.
